text.p: These are some of the main stories in Sofia newspapers on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said foreign currency deposits in commercial banks would be safe even if a currency board system was introduced in the country. Bulgarians have withdrawn some $28 million in foreign currency deposits from commercial banks because of uncertainty over the impact of a currency board, central bank figures show.

-- Commercial banks isolated financial brokerage houses on the interbank forex market as a result of a gentlemens' agreement between the central bank and 10 leading commercial banks last Friday to curb speculation and halt the fall of the lev.

-- Bulgaria, Russia and Greece are expected to sign a tripartite agreement by the end of the year for the construction of the gas pipeline from Bulgaria's Black Sea port of Burgas to Alexandroupolis in Greece, Bulgaria's deputy prime minister Doncho Konakchiev said.
-- Inflation for the period April-December 1997 is expected to be 21-26 percent if a currency board system is introduced early next year, Deputy Prime Minister Roumen Gechev said.

-- Russian Nuclear Energy Minister Viktor Michailov will arrive in Sofia today to discuss the upgrade of Bulgaria's Kozloduy nuclear power station and a possible $200-400 million commodity credit for Bulgaria.
-- State-owned Expressbank is expected to raise its capital by $2.564 million on December 3, a senior bank official said.
-- The central bank will cancel licences of financial houses guilty of illegal financial speculation, Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said.
-- Prime Minister Zhan Videnov said he would resign if the introduction of a currency board system in the country is not successful.
-- BDO Binder won the tender for appointment of an international auditor for the State Savings Bank. The audit is expected to start on November 28 and end on February 15, bank officials said.

-- Bulgaria hopes to receive some $800 million from the International Monetary Fund, the World Bank, G-24 and the European Union as balance of payments support for 1997, Bulgaria's deputy prime minister Roumen Gechev said.
